references.text: Jesus' warning against seeking glory from people instead of from the only God is a direct elaboration of the principle in John 7:18.
Jesus' statement that he does not seek his own glory, but that it is the Father who seeks it, is a direct parallel to the definition of the true speaker in 7:18.
Jesus' confirmation that he has not spoken on his own authority, but only what the Father has given him to say, underscores the absence of injustice in the one who is sent.
Jesus' claim that the words he speaks are not his own, but the Father's who dwells in him, confirms that he does not seek his own glory.
